summary: Edge probe swap during long-lived stream results in missing closing delimiter and partial final paragraph
description:
Issue summary:
Customer reports that during long SSE streams the final closing delimiter ("[DONE]" metadata marker used by their client) is never received after an edge health-check swap. The response body contains the final sentence truncated in the middle of a paragraph.

Impact:
- Intermittent content loss for a small subset of long-running streams (estimated ~0.2% of streams for the affected customer)
- Customer application treats stream as incomplete and triggers retries which double downstream token costs

Environment:
- Redwood hosted API (prod-us-east) hitting edge-gateway cluster behind FastEdge load balancer
- Customer using dedicated account with pinned model redwood-v1-large, streaming via SSE over TLS

Steps to reproduce (customer provided):
1) Open SSE connection using client X with keepalive every 30s
2) Start generation that runs for >45s and includes multi-paragraph output with final delimiter marker
3) Observe that when an edge health-check probe causes connection handover, the client does not receive the final marker and the last paragraph may be cut mid-sentence

Observed behavior:
- Final bytes of the stream appear truncated (cut after a punctuation mark)
- No end-of-stream metadata marker is seen in the SSE stream
- Server logs show connection teardown around the same timestamp as an HTTP/1.1 health probe on the edge node

Expected behavior:
- Stream should include all generated tokens and the closing delimiter metadata event even if the underlying edge connection is rotated or health-probed

Relevant logs/snippet (redacted):
- Customer client trace: "2026-03-12T18:07:12Z SSE CHUNK: "...and finally we recommend updating your policy.""
- Connection closed without [DONE] marker at 2026-03-12T18:07:12.342Z
- Edge proxy log: "probe=health path=/_edge/health reused_conn=false swap_to=10.3.4.22:443 RST_SENT"
- Serving runtime: "session_id=abc123 drain_timeout=0.150 connection_half_closed=true last_kv_commit=1598"

Temporary workaround suggested to customer:
- Short term: switch to a short client-side timeout + polite retry that requests a small context resume (application-level fallback)
- Avoid edge path rewriting by using regional endpoint (us-east.direct.redwood.example) until fix is deployed

Notes:
- Customer supplied multiple traces and the timestamps correlate with edge health-checks that happen every 30s on a subset of our FastEdge fleet
- Not all probes cause the issue; looks correlated with probe that triggers a connection swap while there is in-flight buffered SSE data

investigation_notes: 2026-03-12 20:00 UTC - Reproduced in internal test harness by simulating aggressive healthcheck swap while SSE buffer contains partial JSON payload. The buffer flush path did not complete before the swap; edge sent TCP RST rather than draining gracefully.

Hypothesis A: Edge health-check handler aggressively rotates connections and can trigger RST when out-of-order chunk flush occurs, causing client to miss final delimiter. This will lead to incomplete SSE assembly on client SDKs that expect an explicit end event.

Hypothesis B: Certain TLS session resumption / 0-RTT behavior on the FastEdge node can cause half-close semantics that our serving runtime treats as terminal before emitting the metadata marker. Investigating TLS handshake logs.

Data: Kibana query id=kq-8821 shows 43 events across the cluster matching 'drain_timeout<0.25 && probe_swap=true' between 2026-03-12T17:00 and 2026-03-12T19:00. Grafana dashboard link: https://grafana.redwood.internal/d/streaming/edge-drain?var-node=fastedge
Added additional logging to edge-proxy which records chunk_ack_id and probe_id. Early results show probe_id 0x7a matched with chunk_ack_id left unflushed for affected sessions.

Related: INT-330 contains previous notes about connection reuse heuristics introduced in edge-proxy v2.1.7. That change lowered drain window to favor faster failover under load; might be regression for long-lived streams.
resolution: Root cause: Edge health-check swap could preemptively reset a connection mid-chunk flush. The aggressive connection rotation logic in edge-proxy v2.1.7 reduced the drain grace window; when probe coincided with buffered SSE data, the TCP shutdown semantics caused clients to miss the final metadata marker.

Fix implemented: edge-proxy patch (PR #512) increases drain grace window for streaming endpoints and ensures explicit flush of SSE chunk queue before any RST path is taken. Also added a probe-tag to stream logs for easier correlation.
Rollout plan: canary deploy to 5% FastEdge nodes in us-east on 2026-03-14 02:00 UTC, monitor Kibana query kq-8821 and customer error rate. Full rollout expected 2026-03-15 pending telemetry.
Customer communication: Notified Acme Apps 2026-03-13 with workaround and timeline. Will follow up post-canary and confirm closure once telemetry shows <0.01% occurrence and customer verifies.

Follow-ups: Add a unit/integration test in edge-proxy suite to simulate probe swap during buffered chunk flush. Add runbook entry under Streaming + Edge Troubleshooting. Consider longer-term: better graceful-drain negotiation protocol with serving runtime (RFC ticket).
